notes.notes:

notes.title: Card-based Lovecraftian strategy RPG The Horror at Highrook lands on Steam
notes.notes:
As Darkest Dungeon taught us, the appeal of investigating a sinister mansion infested with Lovecraftian whispers is undeniably tantalizing. I'm therefore compelled to uncover The Horror at Highrook, a new strategy RPG that embraces the card-based management seen in the likes of Cultist Simulator and recent Steam hit Sultan's Game. If 2025 hit Blue Prince has left you with a taste for exploring unusual houses and combining their contents, this new card game is a perfect addition to your wishlist.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Patch 1.04

notes.title: Day 1 Patch ver 1.02
notes.notes:
Hi all,
The launch has gone pretty well, but as to be expected there were a few bugs that managed to evade me before release. I've listed and fixed those below, I'm also fixing any typos and grammatical errors as I go.

Ver 1.02 - quick day 1 patch

Fixed the issue where talking to the ghosts in chapter 5 could leave you stuck in an infinite pause loop. This could happen if you paused the game before clicking on the summoned characters.

Fixed an issue where a new card appearing could push other progression required cards off the task slots (and therefore make them impossible to complete). Again this woudl often get fixed by a exit and reload, but it shouldn't happen now.

Made ember wraiths fixed to their spawn room, but not locked, and also unable to push cards around. They were also the main culprit for the bug above..

Removed an edge case where you could still have a box of wax cylinders hanging about during the ending sequence :)

Fixed some typos and apostrophe errors

notes.title: The Horror At Highrook review
notes.notes:
How’s this for playing yourself: after a week spent clearing out my old family home, a week in which I speedran the lives and deaths of several loved ones by combing through crates of school papers, diaries and letters; with hands wizened by cleaning fluids, nostrils blackened by attic dust, back ruined by the floorboards of my childhood bedroom, and a brain brimming with faded happiness and pain, I sat down in an empty kitchen to play The Horror At Highrook, a cosmic horror table-topper in which four occult investigators scour a vast, cluttered house for the secrets of a missing noble family.

notes.title: Eerie horror card game The Horror at Highrook gets release date, and it's soon
notes.notes:
Despite the fact that the sun is shining and Starbucks is selling its summer-themed iced drinks, I've found myself wandering down the horror hole yet again. From eerie graphic novels to DMing Candela Obscura for my unsuspecting team of paranormal investigators, for whatever reason spring 2025 feels closer to autumn than it does anything else. What better to kick off of my summer spookfest, then, than The Horror at Highrook, a card-based, narrative-driven RPG where solving puzzles and investigation is the name of the game.

notes.title: The Horror AT Highrook - Release Date!
notes.notes:
Hello Investigators,

I'm delighted to announce that The Horror at Highrook will launch on [b]1st May 2025[/b] - Watch the Trailer now!

[url=https://youtu.be/oQIOF6rQfQQ]https://youtu.be/oQIOF6rQfQQ[/url]

As a huge fan of cosmic horror fiction and RPGs, The Horror at Highrook had been bubbling away at the back of my mind for some time. The last few years have been pretty turbulent for indie developers, but I've been lucky enough to be able to keep working on Highrook and bring a long term game dream to life. Now I'm finally on the home stretch and looking forward to sharing the results with you all! It's been fun developing the characters and hearing theories in the Discord from those who have played the demo and beta tests.

As if in some grand cosmic coincidence of announcements The Horror at Highrook is also one of the game featured in the Lovecraftian Days festival - starting today! Even though the full game wont be out until the start of May the demo is still available, and the festival gives me another good opportunity to drum up some attention before the launch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44958602/b21ecbb61fef2707a92efa334edea9daecefda8b.png[/img]

Thanks for all the support so far, can't wait for you all to get your hands on the game!

Much love,

Tom

notes.title: Steam Next Fest
notes.notes:
Greetings Investigator,

Next Fest is upon us, and I'd like to welcome you to the hallowed halls of Highrook Manor. You will be managing your team of intrepid investigators to uncover what happened to the Ackeron family.

Highrook has been a labour of love for me. It's a game that I've always wanted to make and I'm enjoying each layer of polish that I've been adding over these past few months especially. We most recently ran a playtest in December, and I was able to add a whole bunch of recommendations from the community, so huge thank you to everyone who took part!

For those of you who have played previous demos, there's some new things you might like to see!

[list]
[*] New Board Design - The Board of Highrook has been overhauled with unique art. I'm really chuffed with how it looks
[*] New Visual Effects - Atmospheric events and transformations
[*] Dialogue and text overhaul - Less spelling mistakes (I hope)
[*] Tutorial Improvements - Made some tweaks to the tutorial to help with some onboarding!
[*] Quality of Life Improvements - Better guidance, UX and tips
[/list]

If you have any feedback, drop a comment in the Steam Forums or you can join other investigators in the [url=https://discord.gg/z7CV7Bcrw2]Highrook Discord[/url].

I hope you enjoy the demo and thanks very much for playing!

Tom

notes.title: Announcement: Hail the Sloth
notes.notes:
Greetings Investigators!

I've got some exciting news to share with you all today regarding the development of Highrook.

OuterSloth is an indie game development fund created by Innersloth, developers of Among Us. OuterSloth is already funding seven projects, including new games by the developers of Venba, Thirsty Suitors, and I Am Your Beast.

And today, I'm delighted to share that Outersloth have also decided to fund The Horror at Highrook!

This is fantastic news as it's been a rough few years for indies, well, for everyone in the industry really. The Horror at Highrook actually arose as a result of another larger project deal falling through, and it's been a real passion project of mine that had been bubbling away for a few years.

I sent a build of the game to OuterSloth, and it was such a refreshing experience chatting with them. After their success with Among Us, it's reassuring to see a successful indie game re-investing in their own field, especially when the industry seems so unstable. It gives me hope that things might be changing for the better!

I'm making good progress with development, and I'm closing in on the last remaining chapters before polishing begins!

We'll have more on that sooner than you might think, but in the meantime you may wish to join the Highrook Discord and give us a follow on Bluesky for more updates!

Discord Invite: https://discord.gg/XwFcswu4YZ

Bluesky: https://bsky.app/profile/highrookhorror.bsky.social


Will get another one of these written soon!

Cheers,

Tom

notes.title: Demo Update
notes.notes:
I've updated the live demo with a number of bug fixes. I've also added a bunch of features/changes that are part of the main game development so that the demo keeps in line with the rest of the project.

Some of the changes/updates are as follows.

Added larger UI option: Available from the main in game options menu you can now select a larger UI scale to help people playing the game on smaller screens.

Added a character placement slot for room tasks: As pointed out in player feedback, since all tasks require a character card, I've made a specific square in each room for that character. This makes it easier to determine exactly who is carrying out a task.

Card Inspector re-design: a slight redesign of how card info is displayed. This makes it easier to see what type a card is, and where you might be able to use it.

Usage hints and better game guide: Most task items now have a highlighted line at the base of their description, Helping players to work out where to use that task item. The game guide now also features some diagrams/images and reworded text to help explain the mechanics better.

Altered room and Tasks: The Entrance Hall is now The Courtyard, It is still the arrival point for investigators, but it also provides a new primary task "Plunder the Soil" which lets players dig for herbs and other items in the courtyard garden. This change has also effected some of the quest chains for the first chapter.. (mostly to do with how dreams are generated).

Hopefully these changes will make demo even easier to follow and give players a updated idea of how the main game is developing! Thanks for playing, and as usual all feedback is appreciated.. (either on the forums here or via the discord)

notes.title: Demo Available - The First Chapter
notes.notes:
This is the first time that players can open the doors to the cursed manor and start their investigation! The demo features the opening chapter of the game and will allow players to explore early parts of the story and experience the game's many mysterious mechanics.

The Horror at Highrook is an occult card crafting RPG. Explore a haunted mansion with your team of investigators, summon dark entities, craft powerful protections, uncover the fate of a missing family, and choose your own path through the darkness.

This demo is from an in-production build and does not reflect the quality of the final product. 
 It is intended to give you small a taste of the characters, world and gameplay mechanics 
As we continue to develop the game new features will be added and alterations made to existing systems.
If you enjoy the demo please consider wishlisting the game. You can also offer feedback and keep up to date with the development on our discord - follow the links in game or on the store page to join.

Thanks for playing!

notes.title: The Horror At Highrook is an occult cardgame set in a Darkest Dungeon-style mansion
notes.notes:
Earlier today Tom Betts - founder of Nullpointer and former lead programmer at The Signal From Tolva developers Big Robot - emailed me about his new game The Horror At Highrook. In the space of a single, rollercoaster paragraph, Betts earned my curiosity by describing himself as a fellow Soul Reaver enthusiast, lost it again by criticising Soul Reaver’s camera - such insolence! - and earned it swiftly back by mentioning that he’s from Yorkshire. Then, he upgraded my curiosity into attention by describing The Horror At Highrook as a “clockwork narrative” horror experience that takes inspiration from Poe, Stoker and Lovecraft on the one hand, and from boardgames, wiki-hunting and escape rooms on the other.

This is a heady brew indeed. Also, there appears to be a cat in the game called Mr Tubbs, described as a “portly grey barrel of fur”. I entertain suspicions of Mr Tubbs. What fell secrets lurk behind his perfectly groomed exterior? Anyway, here’s the trailer.
